facts.subject: Config
facts.quote: The Pydantic V1 behavior to create a class called Config in the namespace of the parent BaseModel subclass is now deprecated.
facts.explanation: Models should no longer rely on an inner Config class because it is deprecated in V2.

facts.subject: model_config
facts.new_value: a dict with the key/value pairs you want to be used as the config

facts.subject: model_config
facts.quote: When subclassing a model, the model_config attribute is inherited.
facts.explanation: Subclass configuration now propagates automatically, which can affect inherited model behavior.
facts.heading: Changes to config

facts.subject: model_config
facts.new_value: non-default settings are merged; conflicts override with Model2
facts.quote: the non-default settings in the model_config attribute from the two models will be merged, and for any settings defined in both, those from Model2 will override those from Model1 .
facts.explanation: Multiple inheritance can now merge config settings and prefer later bases, which changes effective configuration.
facts.heading: Changes to config

facts.subject: allow_mutation

facts.subject: config
facts.quote: Some of these arguments have been removed from @field_validator in Pydantic V2: config : Pydantic V2’s config is now a dictionary instead of a class, which means this argument is no longer backwards compatible.
facts.explanation: Validator functions can no longer accept config as a signature argument.

facts.subject: config
facts.quote: If you need to access the configuration you should migrate to @field_validator and use info.config .
facts.explanation: Code that accessed validator config must switch to info.config.

facts.subject: field
facts.quote: field : this argument used to be a ModelField object, which was a quasi-internal class that no longer exists in Pydantic V2.
facts.explanation: Validator signatures can no longer rely on the field argument in V2.
facts.heading: Changes to @validator ’s allowed signatures

facts.subject: field
facts.quote: Most of this information can still be accessed by using the field name from info.field_name to index into cls.model_fields
facts.explanation: The guide provides the new way to get field metadata in validators.

facts.subject: TypeError
facts.old_value: converted into a ValidationError in validators
facts.new_value: no longer converted into a ValidationError
facts.quote: TypeError is no longer converted to ValidationError in validators
facts.explanation: Code that used to surface validator TypeErrors as ValidationError will now raise TypeError instead, which can change error handling and user-facing failures.
facts.heading: TypeError is no longer converted to ValidationError in validators

facts.subject: all validation decorators
facts.quote: This applies to all validation decorators.
facts.explanation: The changed exception behavior is not limited to one decorator, so multiple validation entry points may be affected during upgrade.
facts.heading: TypeError is no longer converted to ValidationError in validators

facts.subject: coercing int, float, and Decimal values to strings
facts.quote: coercing int , float , and Decimal values to strings is now optional and disabled by default
facts.explanation: Models that relied on automatic number-to-string coercion will stop getting that conversion unless it is explicitly enabled.
facts.heading: Validator behavior changes

facts.subject: iterable of pairs
facts.new_value: no longer coerced to a dict
facts.quote: iterable of pairs is no longer coerced to a dict.
facts.explanation: Inputs like lists of key-value pairs will no longer be accepted as dict values by coercion, which can break existing parsing code.
facts.heading: Validator behavior changes

facts.subject: allow_reuse
facts.quote: The allow_reuse keyword argument is no longer necessary
facts.explanation: This is a compatibility simplification: existing uses of allow_reuse are usually unnecessary and can be removed.
facts.heading: The allow_reuse keyword argument is no longer necessary

facts.subject: allow_reuse=True
facts.old_value: used to disable false-positive reuse detection
facts.quote: if you were using allow_reuse=True , you should be able to simply delete that keyword argument
facts.explanation: The migration guidance says code using allow_reuse=True can typically be updated by removing the argument.
facts.heading: The allow_reuse keyword argument is no longer necessary

facts.subject: redefinition within a single class
facts.old_value: reused functions were tracked by fully qualified name
facts.new_value: only error for redefinition within a single class
facts.quote: Our approach to detecting repeatedly defined functions has been overhauled to only error for redefinition within a single class
facts.explanation: Decorator reuse detection is narrower now, so some cases that previously errored will no longer do so.
facts.heading: The allow_reuse keyword argument is no longer necessary

facts.subject: @validate_arguments
facts.quote: the @validate_arguments decorator has been renamed to @validate_call .
facts.explanation: Code using the old decorator name must be updated to the new API name.
facts.heading: @validate_arguments has been renamed to @validate_call

facts.subject: @validate_call
facts.old_value: decorated function had attributes such as raw_function and validate
facts.quote: we have not preserved this functionality in @validate_call .
facts.explanation: Code that depended on the extra attributes or validation-only behavior from the old decorator may break after migration.
facts.heading: @validate_arguments has been renamed to @validate_call

facts.subject: input type
facts.old_value: preserved in all cases for generic collections
facts.new_value: only output type is promised to match the annotation
facts.quote: we no longer attempt to preserve the input type in all cases; instead, we only promise that the output type will match the type annotations.
facts.explanation: Applications relying on round-tripping exact collection subclasses may now see plain annotated types instead.
facts.heading: Input types are not preserved

facts.subject: subclasses of BaseModel
facts.quote: we do preserve them for subclasses of BaseModel
facts.explanation: This clarifies an exception to the broader input-type change and indicates BaseModel subclasses keep their concrete type.
facts.heading: Input types are not preserved

facts.subject: dataclasses
facts.quote: and for dataclasses:
facts.explanation: This clarifies that dataclass subclasses still keep their input type under the new behavior.
facts.heading: Input types are not preserved

facts.subject: Iterables of pairs
facts.old_value: valid for fields of type dict
facts.new_value: no longer pass validation for dict fields
facts.quote: Iterables of pairs (which include empty iterables) no longer pass validation for fields of type dict .
facts.explanation: Inputs previously accepted as dicts via pair iteration will now fail validation, which can break deserialization paths.
facts.heading: Dicts
heading_path: Changes to Handling of Standard Types

facts.subject: union types
facts.old_value: V1 short-circuited to the first validating type, e.g. x=1 for int | str
facts.new_value: Pydantic V2 preserves the input type whenever possible and may return x='1' for int | str
facts.quote: In Pydantic V1, the printed result would have been x=1 , since the value would pass validation as an int . In Pydantic V2, we recognize that the value is an instance of one of the cases and short-circuit the standard union validation.
facts.explanation: Code that relied on V1's left-to-right coercion can observe different union results after upgrading.
facts.heading: Unions
heading_path: Changes to Handling of Standard Types

facts.subject: Field(union_mode='left_to_right')
facts.new_value: Use Field(union_mode='left_to_right') to restore V1 left-to-right behavior
facts.quote: To revert to the non-short-circuiting left-to-right behavior of V1, annotate the union with Field(union_mode='left_to_right') .
facts.explanation: This is the documented way to keep old union validation semantics where needed.
facts.heading: Unions
heading_path: Changes to Handling of Standard Types

facts.subject: bump-pydantic
facts.new_value: Install from PyPI and run against your package to help migrate code
facts.quote: You can install the tool from PyPI: pip install bump-pydantic
facts.explanation: The guide provides an optional migration tool that can speed up porting code to Pydantic V2.

facts.subject: field annotations as Optional
facts.old_value: Optional implied not required in V1
facts.new_value: Optional now more closely matches dataclasses: requiredness depends on whether a default is provided

facts.subject: fields annotated as Any

facts.subject: Pydantic V2 regex handling
facts.quote: Pydantic V1 used Python’s regex library. Pydantic V2 uses the Rust regex crate .

facts.subject: Rust regex crate
facts.new_value: look arounds and backreferences are dropped
facts.quote: it’s a completely different approach to regular expressions. In particular, it promises linear time searching of strings in exchange for dropping a couple of features (namely look arounds and backreferences).
facts.explanation: Patterns using lookarounds or backreferences may stop working under the default V2 regex engine.
facts.heading: Patterns / regex on strings
heading_path: Changes to Handling of Standard Types
